label: input token f during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase
explanation: A single-token detector: fires whenever the input token is f in the original phase (t < L), regardless of L, position, or neighbouring tokens. Magnitude is largest at t=0 (max activation), and declines with position (e.g. ~0.8 of max at t=3, ~0.25-0.55 at t=5-7 near the end of long sequences; occasionally silent for f at t=8). Repeated occurrences of f in the same sequence fire somewhat weaker (~0.7-0.86 of max) than the first. Does not fire on any other token, never at the <DEL> step, and essentially not in the copy phase: f fed back as an input during copying gives only tiny activations (<0.12 of max, ~0.03% of mass) at recall_idx 1-2.

issues: Test split matches the report: precision 0.99995, recall 0.995, F1 0.998, mass recall 0.9997.

Missed activations (495 on test, 491 on dev) are all inputs of f in the copy phase. They are tiny (0.01-0.12 of max), carry 0.0% of the mass, and only occur at recall_idx 1-2. This matches the explanation.

There are 5 false positives on each split, all at t=8 (the last original position). They are scattered. Restricting the predicate to t<8 would be wrong, because t=8 f inputs fire about 99.8% of the time (precision 0.998 for the t==8 sub-predicate). Adding t<8 lowers test F1 to 0.985.

The profile shows decay with position: the top examples are at t=0 (1.00), around 0.8-0.88 at t=2-3, and 0.25-0.55 at t=5-7. Repeat f inputs are around 0.70-0.86. Both match the explanation. Firing is flat across L, prev_tok and to_go.
The feature never fires on any non-f input or at <DEL>. The label does not claim more than the predicate covers.
